record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: If X and Y are locally bounded F-spaces and U: X -> Y is a rotation, meaning an isometry with U(0) = 0, must U be linear even without assuming that the F-norms are concave?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 3T• - Is each rotation mapping a locally bounded space onto a locally bounded space linear without the assumption of concavity of norms ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An F-norm on a real vector space $X$ is a function $\|\cdot\|:X\to[0,\infty)$ such that (i) $\|x\|=0$ iff $x=0$; (ii) $\|\alpha x\|=\|x\|$ for every scalar $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=1$; (iii) $\|\alpha_n x_n - \alpha x\|\to 0$ whenever $\alpha_n\to\alpha$ in $\mathbb{R}$ and $\|x_n-x\|\to 0$; and (iv) $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$. An F-space is a complete metric linear space whose topology is given by such an F-norm via $d(x,y)=\|x-y\|$. An F-space $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ is called locally bounded if the origin has a bounded neighborhood; equivalently, $X$ admits a $p$-homogeneous quasi-norm for some $0<p\le 1$. The F-norm $\|\cdot\|$ is called concave if $t\mapsto\|tx\|$ is concave on $[0,\infty)$ for every $x\in X$. A rotation from $X$ to $Y$ is a map $U:X\to Y$ that is an isometry (i.e. $\|U(x)-U(y)\|_Y=\|x-y\|_X$ for all $x,y\in X$) and satisfies $U(0)=0$.

Question: Let $X$ and $Y$ be locally bounded F-spaces and let $U:X\to Y$ be a surjective rotation. Must $U$ be linear, without assuming that the F-norms on $X$ and $Y$ are concave?
artifact.status_search_result: Classical results of Charzyński and Rolewicz establish linearity of surjective isometries fixing the origin in finite-dimensional F-spaces and in locally bounded spaces with concave F-norms. Subsequent work (e.g. Ding–Huang on locally midpoint constricted F-spaces, and generalizations to p-normed spaces) extends linearity under additional structural assumptions, but a definitive resolution of the general locally bounded case without concavity does not appear in the located sources. The problem's current status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: On maps which preserve equality of distance in F-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Charzyński and Rolewicz proved linearity of surjective isometries in finite-dimensional F-spaces and in locally bounded spaces with concave norm.
status_evidence.claim: Known linearity results require concavity or finite-dimensionality assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Mazur–Ulam theorem
status_evidence.snippet: The Mazur–Ulam theorem concerns surjective isometries of normed spaces, with generalizations to various non-locally-convex settings under additional hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: General problem of dropping concavity in locally bounded F-spaces is addressed only under further structural conditions.
